title: Address to Marcianus: one path of faith
english: I know, beloved Marcianus, your zeal for the piety that is toward God — the only road that leads a human being unto life everlasting. ([[life everlasting >> Bible:Jn 3:16]]; [[Mt 19:16 >> Bible:Mt 19:16]]) So I share your joy, and I pray that by keeping the faith whole and unshaken you may be well-pleasing to God who made you. ([[well-pleasing to God >> Bible:Heb 11:6]])

Would that it were granted us to be always together, to help one another, and to lighten the labors of this present life by daily converse on what is profitable! But since at this moment we are parted in body, we will not omit — so far as we are able — to speak with you a little by writing, and to set out briefly the preaching of the truth, for the confirming of your faith. ([[confirming of your faith >> Bible:Lk 22:32]]; [[Acts 16:5 >> Bible:Acts 16:5]])

We send you, as it were, a memorandum of the chief points, that from a little you may reach much: that in a short compass you may grasp the whole body of the truth, and in few words receive the demonstration of the things of God. So it will bear fruit for your own salvation, and you will put to shame all who teach what is false, and with all confidence you will hand on our healthy and pure teaching to everyone who wishes to learn it. ([[healthy teaching >> Bible:1 Tim 1:10]]; [[Tt 1:9 >> Bible:Tt 1:9]]; [[Tt 2:1 >> Bible:Tt 2:1]])

For there is one way that leads upward for all who see, lit with heavenly light; but many and dark and contrary are the ways of those who do not see. This way leads to the kingdom of heaven, joining the human being to God; but those ways bring down to death, separating the human being from God. ([[kingdom of heaven >> Bible:Mt 7:13-14]]; [[Jn 14:6 >> Bible:Jn 14:6]])

Therefore it is necessary for you and for all who care for their own salvation to make your course unswerving, firm, and sure by means of faith, lest you grow slack and be held back among bodily desires, or turn aside and wander from the straight.
notes_covered: one illuminated way vs many dark ways
translator_notes: Copy-text: Armenian PO XII.5 (PDF locked). Readable sense-check: Barthoulot French (PD). Pass B independent of Robinson 1920 / Wilson English.
Inline Logos bible refs on quotes/allusions ([[display >> Bible:…]]).

title: Holiness of body and soul; Psalm 1 triad
english: Now since the human being is a living creature compounded of soul and flesh, it is necessary to take account of both. And since offenses arise from both sides, holiness of the flesh is restraining abstinence from every shameful thing and every unjust deed, and holiness of the soul is keeping faith toward God entire — neither adding to it nor taking from it. ([[neither add nor take away >> Bible:Dt 4:2]]; [[Rev 22:18-19 >> Bible:Rev 22:18-19]])

For piety toward God is withered and stained by the defilement of the flesh, and it is broken and polluted and no longer whole if falsehood enters the soul. But it will keep its own beauty and measure when truth abides in the soul and purity in the flesh.

For what profit is it to know the truth in words, and to pollute the flesh and work the works of evil? Or what profit can purity of the flesh bring, if truth is not in the soul? For these rejoice with one another, and are allied, to set the human being face to face against God.

Therefore the Holy Spirit says through David: ‘Blessed is the man who has not walked in the counsel of the ungodly’ ([[Ps 1:1 >> Bible:Ps 1:1]]) — that is, the counsel of the nations that do not know God; for those are ungodly who do not worship the God who truly is. And therefore the Word says to Moses: ‘I am the One who is.’ ([[Ex 3:14 >> Bible:Ex 3:14]]) But those who do not worship the God who is — these are the ungodly.

‘And has not stood in the way of sinners’ ([[Ps 1:1 >> Bible:Ps 1:1]]): but sinners are those who have knowledge of God and do not keep his commandments — that is, disdainful scorners. ‘And has not sat in the seat of the pestilent’ ([[Ps 1:1 >> Bible:Ps 1:1]]): now the pestilent are those who by wicked and perverse teachings corrupt not only themselves but others also. For a seat is a symbol of teaching. Such then are all heretics: they sit in the seats of the pestilent, and those who receive from them drink in the venom of their doctrine.
translator_notes: Standard §2 = French numbered 1 in Barthoulot. Independent English; Robinson/Wilson check-only.
Inline Logos bible refs ([[display >> Bible:…]]).

title: Rule of faith; baptism into Father, Son, Spirit
english: But we shall not suffer anything of this kind if we hold the rule of the faith without deviation, and do the commandments of God, believing in God and fearing him as Lord and loving him as Father. Now this doing is produced by faith; for Isaiah says: ‘If you do not believe, neither shall you understand.’ ([[Isa 7:9 >> Bible:Isa 7:9]] LXX sense)

And faith is produced by the truth; for faith rests on things that truly are. For in things that are, as they are, we believe; and believing in things that are, as they ever are, we keep firm our confidence in them. Since then faith is the preservation of our salvation, we must bestow much care on maintaining it, that we may have a true comprehension of the things that are.

Now faith occasions this for us, even as the elders, the disciples of the apostles, have handed down to us. First of all it bids us bear in mind that we have received baptism for the remission of sins, in the name of God the Father, and in the name of Jesus Christ, the Son of God, who became incarnate and died and rose again, and in the Holy Spirit of God. ([[baptism … name >> Bible:Mt 28:19]]; [[Acts 2:38 >> Bible:Acts 2:38]]; [[remission of sins >> Bible:Lk 24:47]])

And that this baptism is the seal of eternal life, and is the new birth unto God, that we should no longer be sons of mortal men only, but of the eternal and everlasting God; ([[new birth >> Bible:Jn 3:3-5]]; [[Tt 3:5 >> Bible:Tt 3:5]]) and that what is everlasting and continuing is made God; and is over all things that are made, and all things are put under him; ([[all things under him >> Bible:1 Cor 15:27]]; [[Ps 8:6 >> Bible:Ps 8:6]]) and all the things that are put under him are made his own; for God is not ruler and Lord over the things of another, but over his own; and all things are God’s; and therefore God is Almighty, and all things are of God.
translator_notes: French §3 block; baptismal triad explicit. Independent English.
Inline Logos bible refs ([[display >> Bible:…]]).

title: One unmade Father who makes what was not
english: For it is necessary that things that are made should have the beginning of their making from some great cause; and the beginning of all things is God. For he himself was not made by any, and by him all things were made. ([[all things were made through him >> Bible:Jn 1:3]]; [[Col 1:16 >> Bible:Col 1:16]]; [[Heb 1:2 >> Bible:Heb 1:2]])

And therefore it is right first of all to believe that there is One God, the Father, who made and fashioned all things, and made what was not that it should be, and who, containing all things, alone is uncontained. ([[made what was not >> Bible:Rom 4:17]]; [[2 Macc 7:28 >> Bible:2 Macc 7:28]])
Now among all things is this world of ours, and in the world is the human being: so then this world also was formed by God.
translator_notes: Standard §4; French marker 4. in PO. Independent English.
Inline Logos bible refs ([[display >> Bible:…]]).

title: Word and Spirit: creation, adornment, Pauline triad
english: Thus then there is shown forth One God, the Father, not made, invisible, creator of all things; above whom there is no other God, and after whom there is no other God. ([[no other God >> Bible:Isa 45:5]]; [[Dt 4:35 >> Bible:Dt 4:35]]; [[Dt 6:4 >> Bible:Dt 6:4]])

And since God is rational, therefore by the Word he created the things that were made; and God is Spirit, and by the Spirit he adorned all things: as also the prophet says: ‘By the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and by his spirit all their power.’ ([[Ps 33:6 >> Bible:Ps 33:6]])

Since then the Word establishes — that is, gives body and grants the reality of being — and the Spirit gives order and form to the diversity of the powers, rightly and fittingly is the Word called the Son, and the Spirit the Wisdom of God.

Well also does Paul his apostle say: ‘One God, the Father, who is over all and through all and in us all.’ ([[Eph 4:6 >> Bible:Eph 4:6]]) For over all is the Father; and through all is the Son, for through him all things were made by the Father; and in us all is the Spirit, who cries ‘Abba, Father,’ ([[Rom 8:15 >> Bible:Rom 8:15]]; [[Gal 4:6 >> Bible:Gal 4:6]]) and fashions the human being into the likeness of God. ([[likeness of God >> Bible:Gen 1:26]])

Now the Spirit shows forth the Word, and therefore the prophets announced the Son of God; and the Word utters the Spirit, and therefore is himself the announcer of the prophets, and leads and draws the human being to the Father.
translator_notes: Independent English from French sense-check of Armenian.
Inline Logos bible refs ([[display >> Bible:…]]).

title: Three points of the rule: Father, Word, Spirit
english: This then is the order of the rule of our faith, and the foundation of the building, and the stability of our way of life: God, the Father, not made, not material, invisible; one God, the creator of all things: this is the first point of our faith.

The second point is: the Word of God, Son of God, Christ Jesus our Lord, who was manifested to the prophets according to the form of their prophesying and according to the method of the Father’s economy; through whom all things were made; who also at the end of the times, to complete and gather up all things, was made man among men, visible and tangible, in order to abolish death and show forth life and produce a community of union between God and man. ([[gather up all things >> Bible:Eph 1:10]]; [[abolish death >> Bible:2 Tim 1:10]]; [[Heb 2:14 >> Bible:Heb 2:14]])

And the third point is: the Holy Spirit, through whom the prophets prophesied, and the fathers learned the things of God, and the righteous were led forth into the way of righteousness; and who in the end of the times was poured out in a new way upon humankind in all the earth, renewing the human being unto God. ([[poured out >> Bible:Joel 2:28]]; [[Acts 2:17 >> Bible:Acts 2:17]]; [[Tt 3:5 >> Bible:Tt 3:5]])
translator_notes: Independent English; prior Robinson English not copied.
Inline Logos bible refs ([[display >> Bible:…]]).

title: Baptismal regeneration through the three; knowledge of Father via Son and Spirit
english: And for this reason the baptism of our regeneration proceeds through these three points: God the Father bestowing on us regeneration through his Son by the Holy Spirit. For as many as carry the Spirit of God are led to the Word, that is to the Son; and the Son brings them to the Father; and the Father causes them to possess incorruption. ([[led by the Spirit >> Bible:Rom 8:14]]; [[incorruption >> Bible:1 Cor 15:53-54]])

Without the Spirit it is not possible to behold the Word of God, nor without the Son can any draw near to the Father: for the knowledge of the Father is the Son, and the knowledge of the Son of God is through the Holy Spirit; and, according to the good pleasure of the Father, the Son ministers and dispenses the Spirit to whomsoever the Father wills and as he wills. ([[no one comes to the Father except through me >> Bible:Jn 14:6]]; [[Mt 11:27 >> Bible:Mt 11:27]])
translator_notes: Independent English.
Inline Logos bible refs ([[display >> Bible:…]]).

title: Father as Most High for believers, Jews, Gentiles; judgment
english: And by the Spirit the Father is called Most High and Almighty and Lord of hosts; that we may learn concerning God that he it is who is creator of heaven and earth and all the world, and maker of angels and men, and Lord of all, through whom all things exist and by whom all things are sustained; merciful, compassionate and very tender, good, just, the God of all — both of Jews and of Gentiles, and of those who believe. ([[Most High >> Bible:Ps 7:17]]; [[Lord of hosts >> Bible:Isa 6:3]]; [[God of Jews and Gentiles >> Bible:Rom 3:29]])

To those who believe he is as Father, for in the end of the times he opened up the covenant of adoption; ([[adoption >> Bible:Rom 8:15]]; [[Gal 4:5 >> Bible:Gal 4:5]]) but to the Jews as Lord and Lawgiver, for in the intermediate times, when humankind forgot God and revolted from him, he brought them into subjection by the Law, that they might learn that they had for Lord the maker and creator, who also gives the breath of life, and whom we ought to worship day and night; and to the Gentiles as maker and creator and almighty; and to all alike sustainer and nourisher and king and judge.

For none shall escape and be delivered from his judgment — neither Jew nor Gentile, nor believer that has sinned, nor angel: but they who now reject his goodness shall know his power in judgment, according to that which the blessed apostle says: ‘Not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance; but according to your hardness and impenitent heart you treasure up for yourself wrath in the day of wrath and of the revelation of the righteous judgment of God, who shall render to every one according to his works.’ ([[Rom 2:4-6 >> Bible:Rom 2:4-6]])

This is he who is called in the Law the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, the God of the living; ([[Ex 3:6 >> Bible:Ex 3:6]]; [[Mt 22:32 >> Bible:Mt 22:32]]) although the sublimity and greatness of this God is unspeakable.
translator_notes: Independent English.
Inline Logos bible refs ([[display >> Bible:…]]).

title: Seven heavens; sevenfold Spirit on the Son; menorah pattern
english: Now this world is encompassed by seven heavens, in which dwell powers and angels and archangels, doing service to God, the Almighty and Maker of all things: not as though he were in need, but that they may not be idle and unprofitable and ineffectual.

Wherefore also the Spirit of God is manifold in his indwelling, and in seven forms of service is he reckoned by the prophet Isaiah, as resting on the Son of God, that is the Word, in his coming as man. ‘The Spirit of God,’ he says, ‘shall rest upon him, the Spirit of wisdom and of understanding, the Spirit of counsel and of might, the Spirit of knowledge and of godliness; the Spirit of the fear of God shall fill him.’ ([[Isa 11:2-3 >> Bible:Isa 11:2-3]])

Now the heaven which is first from above, and encompasses the rest, is that of wisdom; and the second from it, of understanding; and the third, of counsel; and the fourth, reckoned from above, is that of might; and the fifth, of knowledge; and the sixth, of godliness; and the seventh, this firmament of ours, is full of the fear of that Spirit which gives light to the heavens.

For, as the pattern of this, Moses received the seven-branched lampstand that shone continually in the holy place; for as a pattern of the heavens he received this service, according to that which the Word spoke unto him: ‘You shall make it according to all the pattern of the things which you have seen on the mountain.’ ([[Ex 25:40 >> Bible:Ex 25:40]]; [[Heb 8:5 >> Bible:Heb 8:5]]; [[seven lamps >> Bible:Ex 25:31-37]])
translator_notes: Independent English; seven-heavens cosmology as in Armenian/French.
Inline Logos bible refs ([[display >> Bible:…]]).

title: Word and Wisdom glorify the Father; cherubim/seraphim; bounds of creation
english: Now this God is glorified by his Word who is his Son continually, and by the Holy Spirit who is the Wisdom of the Father of all; and the powers of these — namely of the Word and of Wisdom — which are called Cherubim and Seraphim, with unceasing voices glorify God; and every created thing that is in the heavens offers glory to God the Father of all. ([[holy, holy, holy >> Bible:Isa 6:3]]; [[Rev 4:8 >> Bible:Rev 4:8]])

He by his Word has created the whole world, and in the world are the angels; and to all the world he has given laws wherein each several thing should abide, and according to that which is determined by God should not pass their bounds, each fulfilling his appointed task. ([[set bounds >> Bible:Ps 104:9]]; [[Job 38:10-11 >> Bible:Job 38:10-11]]; [[Jer 5:22 >> Bible:Jer 5:22]])
translator_notes: Tip §§1–10. Independent English; Robinson/Wilson not copied. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew.
Inline Logos bible refs ([[display >> Bible:…]]).

title: Man formed by God’s hands; breath; dominion; angels in the place
english: But as for the human being — him he formed with his own hands, taking from the earth what was finest and purest, and uniting his own power with the earth in measure. ([[formed … dust of the ground >> Bible:Gen 2:7]]; [[image of God >> Bible:Gen 1:26-27]]) For this purpose he stamped his own likeness upon the formation, so that what was seen might be of divine form: for as the image of God the human being was formed and set on the earth.

And that he might become living, God breathed upon his face the breath of life; and that vivifying breath made the human being like unto God. ([[breathed … breath of life >> Bible:Gen 2:7]]) He was created free and master of his own acts, and was destined by this same God to rule over all that would be upon the earth. ([[rule … over the earth >> Bible:Gen 1:28]])

Great creations in the world had been prepared by God before the human being was made. A place was given to the human being, furnished with all things. In this place God, the maker of all things, had set servants, each with his own particular office. A chiliarch-steward was guardian of the place and was set over his fellow-servants. These servants were angels; and as for the chiliarch-steward, he was an archangel.

title: Man still a child; Paradise prepared; Word walks with him
english: Now God made the human being master of the earth and of all that it contains; he also established him specially as master of those beings who were to serve him. But while these latter were in their full strength, the master — that is, the human being — was still small; he was a child who must necessarily grow in order to reach his perfection.

That he might live and grow in joy and well-being, God had prepared for him the best region of the world as to air, beauty, light, food, plants, fruits, and waters; nothing was lacking of what suits the needs of life. And this place was named Paradise. ([[garden in Eden >> Bible:Gen 2:8-9]])

And so Paradise was fair and good. The Word of God went there every day, walking about, conversing with the human being of things to come, and applying himself above all to make him understand that he would dwell and converse with him, and that he would remain with human beings to teach them righteousness. ([[walked in the garden >> Bible:Gen 3:8]]; [[Word became flesh / dwell >> Bible:Jn 1:14]])
But the human being was a child; he did not yet have the perfect use of his faculties, and so he was easily deceived by the seducer.

title: Naming the animals; Eve from Adam’s rib
english: Now while Adam was walking in Paradise, God, who was there, brought before him all the animals and ordered him to give a name to each; and Adam imposed a name on each of the living creatures. ([[whatever Adam called … that was its name >> Bible:Gen 2:19-20]])

God also resolved to give a helper to the human being; then he spoke thus: ‘It is not good that the human being should be alone; let us make for him a helper like him.’ ([[Gen 2:18 >> Bible:Gen 2:18]]) For among all the living beings there was no helper equal, proportionate, and like Adam.

Now God himself sent an ecstasy upon Adam and put him to sleep; and for the accomplishment of his masterpiece God willed that Adam should fall into sleep, which previously did not exist in Paradise. God took one of Adam’s ribs and re-formed the flesh in its place; and from that rib which he had drawn out he made the woman; then he set her in Adam’s presence. ([[rib … woman >> Bible:Gen 2:21-22]])
At this sight Adam cried: ‘This now is bone of my bones, flesh of my flesh; she shall be called woman, because she comes from a man who is hers.’ ([[Gen 2:23 >> Bible:Gen 2:23]])

title: Naked without shame; childlike innocence
english: Adam and Eve — such is the name of the woman — were naked and they were not ashamed, for they were innocent and had only pure thoughts like those of children; ([[naked … not ashamed >> Bible:Gen 2:25]]) nothing entered their mind and intelligence that could give birth in the soul to evil desires and shameful movements.

It is that then they kept the integrity of their nature, for what had been breathed into them at the moment of creation was a breath of life. Now so long as this breath kept its intensity and its force, it sheltered their thought and spirit from evil. Therefore they were not ashamed if they embraced and exchanged innocent caresses, like children.

title: Law of the tree: immortality kept or mortality if transgressed
english: But so that the human being might not think himself too great and swell with pride, as if he had no master; so that, in his relations with God his creator, he might not mistake the power and liberties given him by overpassing the bounds set for him; and lest, flattering himself in proud thoughts, he should revolt against God — a law was given him by God, to teach him that he has a master, the Lord of all things.

And he set him certain limits, so that if he should keep the commandment of God he should always remain as he was — that is, immortal; but if he should not keep it, he should become mortal and be dissolved into earth from which his formation had been taken. ([[dust you are >> Bible:Gen 3:19]])

Now the commandment was this: ‘Of every tree that is in the Paradise you shall freely eat; but of that tree alone from which is the knowledge of good and evil, of it you shall not eat; for in the day you eat, you shall surely die.’ ([[Gen 2:16-17 >> Bible:Gen 2:16-17]])

title: Disobedience; Satan through the serpent; expulsion
english: This commandment the human being did not keep, but was disobedient to God, being led astray by the angel who, because of the great gifts of God which he had given to the human being, was envious and jealous of him, and both brought himself to nought and made the human being sinful, persuading him to disobey the commandment of God. ([[serpent deceived >> Bible:Gen 3:1-6]]; [[envy of the devil >> Bible:Wis 2:24]])

So the angel, becoming by his falsehood the author and originator of sin, himself was struck down, having offended against God, and the human being he caused to be cast out from Paradise. And because through the guidance of his disposition he apostatized and departed from God, he was called Satan, according to the Hebrew word — that is, Apostate; but he is also called Slanderer (Devil). ([[Satan >> Bible:Job 1:6]]; [[devil / diabolos >> Bible:Rev 12:9]])

Now God cursed the serpent which carried and conveyed the Slanderer; and this malediction came on the beast himself and on the angel hidden and concealed in him, even on Satan. ([[cursed … serpent >> Bible:Gen 3:14-15]]) And humankind he put away from his presence, removing them and making them dwell on the way toward Paradise at that time; because Paradise does not receive the sinful.

title: Toil outside Paradise; Cain kills Abel; Seth raised up
english: Once driven from Paradise, Adam and Eve his wife fell into many afflictions of anxiety and suffering, passing in this world in pain, labors, and groanings. For it was under the rays of the sun that Adam worked the earth, and it brought forth thorns and thistles, the punishment of sin. ([[thorns and thistles >> Bible:Gen 3:17-19]])

Then was fulfilled that which is written: ‘Adam knew his wife, and she conceived and bore Cain; and after him she bore Abel.’ ([[Gen 4:1-2 >> Bible:Gen 4:1-2]]) But the rebel angel who had drawn the human being into disobedience, who had made him a sinner and who had been cause of his expulsion from Paradise, was not content with this first evil; he caused a second to be committed between the two brothers. For, having filled Cain with his spirit, he made him a fratricide. ([[Cain rose up … killed Abel >> Bible:Gen 4:8]])

So Abel died, slain by his brother; and thereby it was signified that some would be persecutors and oppressors and become murderers — but that it would be the wicked who would kill and persecute the righteous. ([[righteous Abel >> Bible:Mt 23:35]]; [[1 Jn 3:12 >> Bible:1 Jn 3:12]]) Thereupon the anger of God grew heavier; he cursed Cain, and it came about that all his race, generation after generation, became like their father. ([[cursed from the ground >> Bible:Gen 4:11-12]]) And God raised up for Adam another son in place of Abel who was slain. ([[Seth … instead of Abel >> Bible:Gen 4:25]])

title: Wickedness spreads; angels and daughters; arts of magic
english: And evil, spreading and propagating more and more, ended by reaching the whole human race, so that there remained among them only some rare seed of righteousness. And indeed unlawful unions took place upon the earth; angels having had commerce with the daughters of the children of men, these bore them children who, because of their extraordinary size, were called sons of the earth (giants). ([[sons of God … daughters of men >> Bible:Gen 6:1-4]])

Now the angels made a present to their wives of lessons of malice, for they taught them the virtues of plants and herbs, the use of colors and cosmetics, the discovery of precious substances, magic, hatreds, loves, passions, evil suggestions, the secrets of sorcery, every kind of divination and the idolatry proper to those who hate God: all this, entering into the world, poured out a torrent of evil, and righteousness went on weakening. ([[taught … charms / idolatry traditions >> Bible:1 Enoch 8]] allusive; [[idolatry >> Bible:Rom 1:23-25]])

title: Flood in the tenth generation; Noah’s ark; Shem Ham Japheth
english: When the justice of God, to chastise the world, unleashed the flood, ten generations after the creation of the first human being, only one just man was found — Noah. ([[Noah … righteous >> Bible:Gen 6:9]]; [[1 Pet 3:20 >> Bible:1 Pet 3:20]]) Because of his righteousness he was saved, and with him his wife and his three sons, and the three wives of his sons; they were shut up in the ark with all the animals that God had designated to Noah to bring in with him. ([[ark >> Bible:Gen 7:1-16]])

And as the destroying scourge had extended to all — to human beings and even to the animals that were upon the earth — the stock of these beings was preserved in the ark. The three sons of Noah were Shem, Ham, and Japheth, by whom the race was multiplied again; they were the stem of humankind after the flood. ([[Gen 9:18-19 >> Bible:Gen 9:18-19]])

title: Ham cursed; Shem and Japheth blessed; Gentile calling foreshadowed
english: But one of them fell under the stroke of curses; the other two inherited the blessing because of their works. For the younger of them, called Ham, mocked his father; and because of the insult and contempt shown to his father he was condemned for a sin of impiety and cursed, and he made the curses fall back upon all who were born of him: so it came about that all his race after him was cursed, grew, and multiplied in sin. ([[cursed be Canaan >> Bible:Gen 9:22-25]])

On the contrary, Shem and Japheth, his brothers, because of their filial piety toward their father, were loaded with blessings. Now the curse of Ham, launched against him by his father Noah, was this: ‘Cursed be the child of Ham; let him be the servant of his brothers!’ ([[Gen 9:25 >> Bible:Gen 9:25]]) His children had a numerous posterity upon the earth; for fourteen generations it developed in their land, until the day when it was harvested by God, who made it undergo his judgment.

And just as the curse passed on, so also the blessing passed on to the race of him who was blessed, each in his order. For first Shem was blessed in these words: ‘Blessed be the Lord, the God of Shem; and Ham shall be his servant.’ ([[Gen 9:26 >> Bible:Gen 9:26]]) The power of the blessing lies in this — that the God and Lord of all should be to Shem a peculiar possession of worship. And the blessing extended and reached unto Abraham, who was reckoned as descended in the tenth generation from the race of Shem. ([[genealogy Shem to Abram >> Bible:Gen 11:10-26]])

Now the blessing of Japheth is on this wise: ‘God shall enlarge unto Japheth, and he shall dwell in the house of Shem, and Ham shall be his servant.’ ([[Gen 9:27 >> Bible:Gen 9:27]]) That is: at the end of the ages he blossomed forth, at the appearing of the Lord, through the calling of the Gentiles, when God enlarged unto them the calling; and their sound went out into all the earth, and their words to the end of the world. ([[Rom 10:18 >> Bible:Rom 10:18]]; [[Ps 19:4 >> Bible:Ps 19:4]]) The enlarging, then, is the calling from among the Gentiles — that is, the Church — and Japheth’s dwelling in the house of Shem signifies dwelling in the inheritance of the fathers, having received in Jesus Christ the rights of the firstborn. ([[Gentiles … fellow heirs >> Bible:Eph 3:6]]; [[firstborn among many brothers >> Bible:Rom 8:29]])

title: Blessing of Shem to Abraham; Japheth and the nations
english: Just as the curse ran its course, so the blessing spread abroad upon the blessed line, each according to his order. First among them Shem was blessed in these words: ‘Blessed be the Lord, the God of Shem; and Ham shall be his servant.’ ([[Gen 9:26 >> Bible:Gen 9:26]]) The force of that blessing is this: that God, the Lord of all, became the privileged possession of Shem’s piety.

That blessing flowered when it reached Abraham, who stands tenth in the genealogy counted down from Shem’s seed. ([[Shem to Abram >> Bible:Gen 11:10-26]]) For this reason the Father and God of all was pleased to be named the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob — for upon Abraham the blessing of Shem had come to rest. ([[God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob >> Bible:Ex 3:6]]; [[Mt 22:32 >> Bible:Mt 22:32]])

And the blessing of Japheth runs thus: ‘May God enlarge Japheth, and let him dwell in the house of Shem; and let Ham be his servant.’ ([[Gen 9:27 >> Bible:Gen 9:27]]) That is: this blessing came into bloom at the end of the ages, when the Lord was manifested in the calling of the Gentiles, God having stretched his call out to them. For ‘their voice went out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.’ ([[Ps 19:4 >> Bible:Ps 19:4]]; [[Rom 10:18 >> Bible:Rom 10:18]])

‘Enlarge,’ then, means the calling of the nations — that is, the Church; and ‘Japheth shall dwell in the house of Shem’ means that he shall dwell in the fathers’ inheritance, having received in Jesus Christ the rights of the firstborn. ([[Gentiles fellow heirs >> Bible:Eph 3:6]]; [[firstborn >> Bible:Rom 8:29]]) And each, according to the order in which he was blessed, receives by descent the fruit of the blessing.

title: Noahic covenant: rainbow, meat, blood; image of God
english: But after the flood God bound himself by oath toward the whole world — above all toward living creatures and human beings — that he would never again destroy by a flood whatever would spring up on the earth; and he set them a sign: ‘When I cover the sky with a cloud, the bow shall appear in the cloud, and I will remember the oath of my covenant, and I will no more destroy by water all flesh that moves upon the earth.’ ([[Gen 9:14-15 >> Bible:Gen 9:14-15]])
He also changed human food, granting permission to eat flesh; for from Adam’s making until the flood people lived on seeds and the fruit of trees, and flesh was not allowed them.

Since Noah’s three sons were the stock of the human race, God blessed them to increase and multiply, saying: ‘Increase and multiply and fill the earth and rule it. The fear and dread of you shall be upon every living creature of the earth and every bird of the sky; and they shall be food for you, even as the green plants. Only you shall not eat flesh with its life-blood. And your own blood I will require at the hand of every beast and of man. Whoever sheds the blood of a human being, by a human being shall his blood be shed; for God made the human being in his image.’ ([[Gen 9:1-6 >> Bible:Gen 9:1-6]])

Now the image of God is the Son, after whose likeness the human being was made. ([[image of God >> Bible:Gen 1:26-27]]; [[Col 1:15 >> Bible:Col 1:15]]) And for this reason he appeared at the end of the ages, to show that his image is like him. After this covenant the race from those three sons multiplied; and the earth had one lip — that is, one language. ([[one language >> Bible:Gen 11:1]])

title: Babel: one tongue divided; races scattered
english: Then people rose and left the lands of the East; and as they went forward upon the earth they came to the broad plain of Shinar. ([[Gen 11:2 >> Bible:Gen 11:2]]) There they set about building a tower by which they hoped to climb to heaven, leaving a monument to keep their memory among later generations. The structure was of burnt brick and asphalt. ([[Gen 11:3-4 >> Bible:Gen 11:3-4]])
Their daring arrogance grew the more because they shared one purpose and lived in one place, and because a single language powerfully furthered the design they had fixed.

But God, unwilling that the work should be finished, divided their languages so that they could no longer understand one another. ([[Gen 11:7-8 >> Bible:Gen 11:7-8]]) So they were split, scattered, and took possession of the world. They dwelt in clans and tribes, each according to its own tongue: hence so many peoples and languages upon the earth.

And since three races of humankind took the earth, and one of them lay under the curse while two had been blessed, the first blessing belonged to Shem, whose posterity dwelt in the East and occupied the land of the Chaldeans. ([[Ur of the Chaldeans >> Bible:Gen 11:28-31]])

title: Abraham seeks God; call, promise, faith, circumcision
english: Later — that is, in the tenth generation after the flood — we find Abraham seeking God, returning to him and belonging to him because of the blessing of his forefather. According to the bent and desire of his soul he went through the world asking where God was; and when he was near to growing weary in the search, God took pity on the only one who sought him in secret. He showed himself to Abraham through the Word, as by a ray of light, and made himself known.

For from heaven he spoke to him and said: ‘Go out from your country and your kindred and your father’s house; come into the land that I will show you, and dwell there.’ ([[Gen 12:1 >> Bible:Gen 12:1]]) Trusting the heavenly voice — though already mature, seventy years old, and married — he went out from Mesopotamia with his wife, taking with him Lot, the son of his dead brother.

And when he had come into the land now called Judea, then inhabited by seven peoples of Ham’s race, God appeared to him again and said: ‘I will give this land to you and to your seed after you for an everlasting possession.’ ([[Gen 12:7 >> Bible:Gen 12:7]]; [[Gen 13:15 >> Bible:Gen 13:15]]) He also announced that his seed would be sojourners in a land not their own, afflicted and enslaved there four hundred years; and in the fourth generation they would return to the land promised to Abraham, for God had judged the nation that had enslaved his seed. ([[Gen 15:13-16 >> Bible:Gen 15:13-16]])

And that Abraham might know not only the fruitfulness but also the glory of his race, God brought him out of his tent by night and said: ‘Look up to heaven and count the stars, if you are able; so shall your seed be.’ ([[Gen 15:5 >> Bible:Gen 15:5]]) Seeing that Abraham did not waver but believed with his whole soul, God bore him witness by the Holy Spirit in the Scripture: ‘Abraham believed, and it was counted to him for righteousness.’ ([[Gen 15:6 >> Bible:Gen 15:6]]; [[Rom 4:3 >> Bible:Rom 4:3]]) He was still uncircumcised when that witness was given. And that the excellence of his faith might be known by a sign, God gave him circumcision, the seal of the righteousness of faith which he had while uncircumcised. ([[Rom 4:11 >> Bible:Rom 4:11]])

Afterward Sarah, who was barren, bore him a son, Isaac, according to God’s promise; and he circumcised him according to the covenant God had made; and Isaac begot Jacob. So the ancient blessing granted to Shem at the beginning was handed on to Abraham, and from Abraham to Isaac, and from Isaac to Jacob, by the Spirit who made them sharers in the inheritance. Therefore God was called the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. ([[Ex 3:6 >> Bible:Ex 3:6]]) And Jacob begot twelve sons, who gave their names to the twelve tribes of Israel.

title: Egypt, Passover lamb, Red Sea; Christ foreshadowed
english: Famine fell upon the whole earth, and it came about that food remained only in Egypt. Then Jacob left his country and went with all his household to dwell in Egypt. The number of those who went down was seventy-five persons; and in four hundred years, as the oracle had foretold, they grew to six hundred and sixty thousand. ([[Gen 46:27 >> Bible:Gen 46:27]]; [[Acts 7:14 >> Bible:Acts 7:14]]; [[Ex 12:37 >> Bible:Ex 12:37]])

And when they were crushed with afflictions and harsh slavery, and groaned and cried out to God — the God of their fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — that same God brought them out of Egypt by Moses and Aaron, and struck the Egyptians with ten plagues. ([[Ex 3:7-10 >> Bible:Ex 3:7-10]]; [[Ex 7–12 >> Bible:Ex 7:1]]) The last plague was to send a destroying angel who slew all the firstborn, of people and of beasts. ([[Ex 12:29 >> Bible:Ex 12:29]])

Thus he saved the children of Israel’s life, and he mysteriously revealed the passion of Christ by commanding that a spotless lamb be slain, whose blood the Hebrews were to put upon the doors of their houses and so be kept from the stroke. ([[Passover lamb >> Bible:Ex 12:3-13]]; [[1 Cor 5:7 >> Bible:1 Cor 5:7]]; [[Jn 1:29 >> Bible:Jn 1:29]]) And the name of that mystery is the Passion, the cause of deliverance.

God also divided the Red Sea and by every means led the children of Israel into the wilderness. ([[Ex 14:21-22 >> Bible:Ex 14:21-22]]) But the Egyptians who pursued them and entered the sea as well all perished. So God punished those who had unjustly mistreated Abraham’s seed.

title: Law, tabernacle, priesthood in the wilderness
english: And in the wilderness Moses received from God the Law — the ten commandments written by the finger of God on tablets of stone (in the Holy Spirit), and then the statutes of the Law and the judgments he ordered the children of Israel to keep. ([[Ex 31:18 >> Bible:Ex 31:18]]; [[Dt 9:10 >> Bible:Dt 9:10]]; [[finger of God >> Bible:Lk 11:20]])

And at God’s command he made the tabernacle, a visible work on earth after the pattern of what is spiritual and invisible in heaven — a figure of the Church and a prophecy of things to come. ([[Ex 25:40 >> Bible:Ex 25:40]]; [[Heb 8:5 >> Bible:Heb 8:5]]) It held the vessels, the altars, and the ark with the tablets.

He also appointed priests — Aaron and his sons — and entrusted the priesthood to their whole house: they were of Levi’s line. ([[Ex 28:1 >> Bible:Ex 28:1]]) By God’s order he set that same tribe to serve in the worship of God’s temple. He gave them the Levitical law to show the qualities and conduct required of those continually occupied in ministry in God’s house.

title: Spies; Hosea renamed Jesus; forty years for unbelief
english: And when the Hebrews drew near the land God had promised to Abraham and his seed, Moses chose one man from each tribe and sent them to spy out the land, its cities, and their inhabitants. ([[Num 13:1-3 >> Bible:Num 13:1-3]]) Then God revealed to him the name of the One who alone can save all who believe in him. Moses therefore changed the name of Hosea son of Nun, one of those sent, and named him Jesus; then he sent him in the full strength of that name, persuaded that under its protection they would return safe — as indeed they did. ([[Num 13:16 >> Bible:Num 13:16]]; [[name of Jesus >> Bible:Acts 4:12]])

When the spies came back from their search, bringing a cluster of grapes, some of the twelve terrified the whole assembly, saying they had found very great cities fortified with walls, and that the people of those lands were giants, sons of giants, so that it was impossible to master the country. ([[Num 13:23-33 >> Bible:Num 13:23-33]]) Then all the people wept, doubting whether God would give them strength and put all under their power. They added that the wicked land was not worth facing so many dangers to conquer it.

But two of the twelve — Jesus son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh — seeing the harm of those words, tore their clothes and pleaded with the people not to lose heart, because God had given those nations into their hands and because the land was exceedingly fertile. ([[Num 14:6-9 >> Bible:Num 14:6-9]]) The people would not be persuaded but persisted in unbelief; so God turned and changed their route and made them wander in the wilderness to test and chastise them.

And as the spies had spent forty days going to explore the land and return, so God, appointing a year for each day, kept them forty years in the wilderness. ([[Num 14:33-34 >> Bible:Num 14:33-34]]) None of those of full age and sound mind was judged worthy to enter that land because of unbelief — except the two who had given a true witness to the promised inheritance, Jesus son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, and those still too small to know their right hand from their left. ([[Heb 3:18-19 >> Bible:Heb 3:18-19]]) The whole unbelieving people perished and wasted away in the wilderness, little by little paying the penalty of their unbelief. But through those forty years the children multiplied until they filled the gaps left by their fathers’ death.

title: Deuteronomy: second law; prophecies of Christ and nations
english: When the forty years were ended, the people came near the Jordan and, gathering together, pitched camp opposite Jericho. ([[Num 22:1 >> Bible:Num 22:1]]; [[Dt 1:1-5 >> Bible:Dt 1:1-5]]) There Moses assembled the multitude and recapitulated all that had happened. He told the wonders God had done until then — how he had raised up those who had multiplied in the wilderness and formed them to fear God and keep his commandments.

All this became for them a kind of new legislation, added to what they had before. This is what is called Deuteronomy, which holds many prophecies concerning our Lord Jesus Christ, concerning the people of Israel, concerning the calling of the Gentiles, and concerning the kingdom. ([[prophet like Moses >> Bible:Dt 18:15-19]]; [[Acts 3:22-23 >> Bible:Acts 3:22-23]])

title: Moses dies; Jesus son of Nun; Jerusalem and Temple
english: And when Moses had finished the course of his life, it was said to him from God: ‘Go up this mountain and die; for you shall not bring my people into this land.’ ([[Dt 32:48-52 >> Bible:Dt 32:48-52]]; [[Dt 34:1-5 >> Bible:Dt 34:1-5]]) Moses died according to the word of the Lord, and Jesus son of Nun succeeded him.

He divided the Jordan, led the people into the promised land, and after subduing and destroying the seven peoples who lived there, he portioned it out to the people. ([[Josh 3–4 >> Bible:Josh 3:1]]; [[Josh 11:23 >> Bible:Josh 11:23]])

There is Jerusalem, where David reigned and Solomon his son. Solomon built the Temple for God’s honor, taking as model the tabernacle Moses had made after the pattern of heavenly and spiritual realities. ([[2 Sam 5:5-9 >> Bible:2 Sam 5:5-9]]; [[1 Kgs 6 >> Bible:1 Kgs 6:1]]; [[Heb 8:5 >> Bible:Heb 8:5]])

title: Prophets announce Christ: Son of David and Son of God
english: There God sent the prophets, who under the inspiration of the Holy Spirit rebuked the people and turned them back to the God of their fathers, the Almighty. ([[2 Chr 24:19 >> Bible:2 Chr 24:19]]; [[Neh 9:26 >> Bible:Neh 9:26]])

In their oracles they announced the manifestation of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, saying that he would spring up as a shoot from the race of David, that according to the flesh he would be son of David, descending from Abraham through a long line of generations. ([[Isa 11:1 >> Bible:Isa 11:1]]; [[Rom 1:3 >> Bible:Rom 1:3]]; [[Mt 1:1 >> Bible:Mt 1:1]])

According to the Spirit he would be Son of God, being in the beginning with his Father, begotten before the foundation of the world, and manifested to the whole universe as man at the end of the ages — the Word of God who was to recapitulate in himself all things in heaven and on earth. ([[Jn 1:1-2 >> Bible:Jn 1:1-2]]; [[Eph 1:10 >> Bible:Eph 1:10]]; [[Col 1:16-20 >> Bible:Col 1:16-20]])
